newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile welcomes court order against Norwegian boat.
newsitem.headline: Chile welcomes court order against Norwegian boat.

text.p: Chile welcomed on Tuesday a court ruling barring a huge Norwegian-built trawler from fishing in Chilean waters after a campaign by ecologists who claimed the ship would decimate dwindling fish stocks.

Norwegian-owned fishing company Pesquera Yelcho had appealed a government decision to reject its application to replace three smaller boats whose fishing licences had expired with the factory ship American Monarch.

"The fishing law bans new factory ships from operating in Chile. The only thing the law did was to make it possible for boats which were already operating (here) to continue fishing," said Fisheries Undersecretary Juan Manuel Cruz.
The court ruled on Monday in favour of the government which had rejected in November plans by Pesquera Yelcho to bring the huge ship to Chile.
American Monarch -- the world's largest factory boat -- can process up to a 1,000 tonnes of fish a day and was expected to work in the rich fishing grounds close to Chile's southern tip.
The court ruling recognized the government's duty to conserve fish stocks and make sure the fishing industry was sustainable in the long-term, said Cruz.
Cruz said he was confident the order would not cause any conflict with Norway and would not affect investments by Chilean and foreign companies in the fishing industry.
"The most likely result on an international level is that the ruling will benefit Chile as we are showing that Chilean law is applied strictly," he said.

After Chile's refusal to accept the ship, Pesquera Yelcho had tried to take the American Monarch to fish in Argentina, South Africa and Russia but none of these countries gave the ship permission to operate, said Cruz.

Greenpeace, which led the campaign against the American Monarch, said heavy fishing by the boat could lead to the destruction of stocks of two species of fish listed in a recent official report as being in danger of extinction.
